preamble: The velar nasal [ŋ] shifting to the bilabial nasal [m] is a change of place from velar to labial. The clearest case is in Romanian, where Latin ⟨gn⟩, pronounced [ŋn], became [mn]: lignum > lemn 'wood', signum > semn 'sign', cognatus > cumnat 'brother-in-law'. Dalmatian has a parallel form (comnut 'brother-in-law'). Romanian shows the same velar-to-labial shift in ct > pt (Latin lac, lactis > lapte 'milk').

examples.note: Latin ⟨gn⟩ stood for [ŋn]; in Romanian the velar nasal became bilabial before /n/.
Dalmatian comnut shows the same outcome.
